title: afs use cases
description: What a coding agent and a developer do with afs, step by step.

entities.name: Re-read a file and get only what changed
entities.description: A coding agent reads a whole file, and later reads it again after it may have changed.
entities.goal: Know a file's current content without receiving again what it already has.
preconditions: The agent talks to one long-lived afs session: `afs serve` through its MCP client, or `afs jsonl`.
The running user may read the file.
postconditions: The agent holds the file's current content: its earlier reply, that reply with the hunks applied, or the new full content.
The session records the etag the agent now has for that path.

flow.action: Calls afs_read with the file's path and no ranges.
Loads the file, records its stamp and etag, keeps its bytes as a diff base, and sends the lines with the etag and a ref; the version counts as fully received when no cap cut it.
Later calls afs_read with the same path again.
Takes the recorded etag when the file's stamp equals the recorded one and was already outside the 2-second racy window when it was recorded; otherwise reloads and hashes the file.
The etag differs: computes line hunks against the version the agent fully received and sends them with changed, base_etag and a new ref.
Applies the hunks to its earlier copy, from the last `at` to the first.

alternatives.condition: The path is missing, unreadable or not a regular file.
alternatives.outcome: An error reply (isError over MCP); nothing is recorded.

alternatives.condition: The file has a NUL byte in its first 8000 bytes.
alternatives.outcome: binary: true and the size, with no lines.

alternatives.condition: The file is longer than max_lines or max_bytes.
alternatives.outcome: truncated, next_ranges and bytes_omitted; the agent continues with ranged reads, and this version is not a diff base for later whole-file reads.

alternatives.condition: The etag is the one this session already sent for the same path, ranges and caps.
alternatives.outcome: {etag, unchanged: true, ref}: the content is in the agent's earlier result with that ref.
The whole content again, without a diff.

alternatives.condition: No fully received earlier version is held (never complete, or evicted from the 64 MiB store), either version is not UTF-8, or the hunks are not under half the file's size.
alternatives.outcome: The whole file, as on a first read.

entities.name: Find a definition and read only it
entities.description: A coding agent outlines source files and reads the line range of the item it needs.
entities.goal: Read one function, type or section without reading the files around it.
preconditions: The agent can call afs as an MCP tool, through `afs jsonl` or with `afs call`.
The files are in a language outline supports.
postconditions: The agent holds the item's lines and their etag.

flow.action: Calls afs_outline with the paths to look in.
Walks the paths honouring ignore files, parses every supported file in parallel and returns [start, end, kind, name] per symbol, sorted by path, caching the result with the walk's stamps.
Calls afs_read with the file and ranges [[start, end]] from the symbol's row.
Returns that range as one chunk with the file's etag and a ref.

alternatives.outcome: An error reply naming the path.
truncated, with total_symbols; the agent narrows the paths.

alternatives.condition: The same outline was already sent and nothing it depends on changed.
The range is longer than the caps.
alternatives.outcome: truncated and next_ranges for the rest.

entities.name: Run a request from the terminal
entities.description: A developer runs one request, or a batch, with `afs call` and reads the JSON reply.
entities.goal: Read, search, list, stat or outline files as JSON from a shell or script, and tell from the exit code whether it worked.
preconditions: afs is installed and on the PATH.
postconditions: The reply is on stdout; the exit code is 0 only if every reply has ok: true.

flow.action: Runs `afs call '<json>'`, or pipes the JSON into `afs call` or `afs call -`.
Parses the JSON and runs the request, or each request of an array in order, in a fresh session.
Prints the reply on one line and exits 0.

alternatives.outcome: All replies are printed and the exit code is 1.
